headline: Metagenome-derived metabolic models guide in silico design of probiotic communities
label: Genome Scale Metabolic Modeling
summary: Metagenomes from fermented beverages and untreated wastewater expand uncharacterized microbial genomes for metabolic modeling and biocontrol safety assessment.
synthesis: The common thread is genome-resolved analysis of microbial metagenomes and whole-genome sequences to characterize function and safety at the genome scale. The fermented-beverage study recovers biosynthetic diversity from kefir, kombucha, pozol and pulque metagenomes and applies genome-scale metabolic modeling to design a six-member probiotic synthetic community in silico. The wastewater study mines 1,344 public metagenomes from six continents for uncharacterized prokaryotic lineages, and the RATION-GUI workflow applies WGS-based QC, taxonomy, AMR and pathogenicity screening to hazard assessment of bacterial and fungal biocontrol agents. The dominant thread is thus sequence-derived genome content. What is new is the explicit use of metagenome-derived metabolic models to propose a defined synthetic community computationally.
